title: Firewall rules: tags, service accounts and priority order

videos.script: A firewall rule in Google Cloud is not a box in the path. It is enforced at every machine's own interface. {{where}} So two machines in the same subnet are filtered from each other exactly as from the internet. {{same}} A rule has a direction, an action, ports, sources, targets, and a priority. The lowest number is read first. {{priority}} At the same number, deny wins over allow. {{tie}} Under everything sit two rules you cannot delete. Deny all that comes in. Allow all that goes out. {{implied}} Now the targets. A rule can name its machines by a tag, or by the service account they run as. {{targets}} A tag is a word anyone who can edit the machine can add. A service account needs a role on the account itself. So the planner opens doors by account, and uses tags only to close them. {{accounts}} Then you walk seven packets through the planner's rules, with a short program that reads them in Google's order. {{end}}
